guarantees.claim: For each instance i from 0 to NumLcSyncCopies-1, lc_escalate_en[i] is assigned the value of lc_ctrl_pkg::lc_tx_or_hi(alert_to_lc_tx, lc_escalate_en_sync[i]).

assumptions.claim: alert_to_lc_tx must be synchronous to the local clock domain (or already synchronized) so that its value is stable when sampled by the combinational lc_tx_or_hi function, preventing metastability on lc_escalate_en.
assumptions.cond: always when lc_escalate_en is used downstream
assumptions.risk: An asynchronous alert_to_lc_tx could cause glitches or metastable values on lc_escalate_en, possibly triggering spurious life‑cycle escalation enable assertions.

formal.consequent: alert_to_lc_tx is stable relative to the local clock

formal_sketch.antecedent: always when lc_escalate_en is used downstream
formal_sketch.consequent: alert_to_lc_tx is stable relative to the local clock

uncertain_points.claim: The exact logic of lc_ctrl_pkg::lc_tx_or_hi is unknown; it may contain masking, priority encoding or gating that affects how alert_to_lc_tx and lc_escalate_en_sync[i] combine to produce lc_escalate_en[i].
uncertain_points.risk: An incorrect or overly permissive combination could prevent the escalation from being asserted or de‑asserted when a real alert is present, weakening security.

formal_sketch.consequent: The exact logic of lc_ctrl_pkg::lc_tx_or_hi is unknown; it may contain masking, priority encoding or gating that affects how alert_to_lc_tx and lc_escalate_en_sync[i] combine to produce lc_escalate_en[i]

uncertain_points.claim: The parameter NumLcSyncCopies must match the declared width of lc_escalate_en and lc_escalate_en_sync; a mismatch could leave bits undriven or cause a multi‑driver conflict.
uncertain_points.cond: NumLcSyncCopies set incorrectly relative to array width
uncertain_points.risk: Undriven lc_escalate_en bits may float or retain old values, leading to partial or missing escalation enables and a possible security bypass.

formal_sketch.antecedent: NumLcSyncCopies set incorrectly relative to array width
formal_sketch.consequent: The parameter NumLcSyncCopies must match the declared width of lc_escalate_en and lc_escalate_en_sync; a mismatch could leave bits undriven or cause a multi‑driver conflict

security_implications: The lc_escalate_en output is a life‑cycle escalation enable signal, likely gating a path that can permanently escalate or restrict device debug. It is derived from alert_to_lc_tx and a synchronized enable through an opaque combinational function. Any glitch, incorrect combination, or parameter mismatch could falsely assert escalation when no real alert exists, or mask a legitimate alert, directly compromising life‑cycle security and access control.
